title: The Picard obstruction exact sequence for an arbitrary square-zero thickening
statement: Let $j:Z\hookrightarrow Z\prime$ be a first order thickening of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-first-order-thickening], with quasi-coherent ideal $I=\ker(\mathcal O_{Z\prime}\to j_*\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Since $I^2=0$, regard $I$ as an $\mathcal O_Z$-module through $\mathcal O_{Z\prime}/I=\mathcal O_Z$. For any scheme $W$, write $\operatorname{Pic}(W)$ for the group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_W$-modules under tensor product [def-sc-invertible-module]. There is a canonical group homomorphism $\delta:\operatorname{Pic}(Z)\to H^2(Z,I)$ such that the sequence $\operatorname{Pic}(Z\prime)\xrightarrow{j^*}\operatorname{Pic}(Z)\xrightarrow{\delta}H^2(Z,I)$ is exact at $\operatorname{Pic}(Z)$ [def-pc-module-pullback, pqf-def-cohomology]. The first map is restriction of invertible modules; $H^2$ is ordinary structure-sheaf module cohomology. Neither scheme is assumed Noetherian, proper, reduced, or finite dimensional.

source.place: Tag 0C6R, lemma-picard-group-first-order-thickening, middle and final displayed rows.

proof.text: By [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], $j$ identifies the underlying spaces of $Z$ and $Z\prime$. Denote the ideal regarded as an $\mathcal O_Z$-module by $I_Z$. Its underlying additive sheaf satisfies $j_*I_Z=I_{\mathrm{ab}}$: the quotient action is well defined since multiplying an element of $I$ by another element of $I$ gives zero. Here $I_{\mathrm{ab}}$ is the underlying additive sheaf of the ideal in [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf].

On this common space there is a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves $0\to I_{\mathrm{ab}}\xrightarrow{a\mapsto1+a}\mathcal O_{Z\prime}^{\times}\xrightarrow{u_j}j_*\mathcal O_Z^{\times}\to0$, with $u_j$ the restriction of [def-sc-zariski-units-restriction]. Indeed $(1+a)(1+b)=1+(a+b)$ and $(1+a)^{-1}=1-a$ since $I^2=0$; the kernel of $u_j$ consists exactly of these units, uniquely. For local surjectivity, lift a unit and its inverse locally to $u,v$ using the surjective structure-sheaf map in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $uv=1+a$ for $a\in I$ by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], so $v(1-a)$ is an inverse for $u$. This is local lifting, and asserts no surjectivity on global sections.

source.place: Tag 0C6R, lemma-picard-group-first-order-thickening, short exact sequence and map f to 1+f

proof.text: Apply the natural long exact cohomology sequence for abelian sheaves in [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology] to Step 2. It provides a canonical homomorphism $\partial:H^1(Z\prime,j_*\mathcal O_Z^{\times})\to H^2(Z\prime,I_{\mathrm{ab}})$ with $\operatorname{im}H^1(u_j)=\ker\partial$. All cohomology groups in this step are abelian-sheaf cohomology on the Zariski topological space, so this is not an application of module cohomology to sheaves of units.

Let $\alpha_W:\operatorname{Pic}(W)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^1(W,\mathcal O_W^{\times})$ be the abelian-group isomorphism of [thm-sc-hilbert-90], for $W=Z,Z\prime$. By [lem-sc-cohomology-closed-immersion-pushforward] the closed immersion $j$ gives isomorphisms $c^1:H^1(Z\prime,j_*\mathcal O_Z^{\times})\xrightarrow{\sim}H^1(Z,\mathcal O_Z^{\times})$ and $c^2:H^2(Z\prime,j_*I_Z)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^2(Z,(I_Z)_{\mathrm{ab}})$. The latter followed by [lem-sc-module-abelian-zariski-cohomology] gives $\beta:H^2(Z\prime,I_{\mathrm{ab}})\xrightarrow{\sim}H^2(Z,I_Z)$ in ordinary module cohomology. The map compatibility [lem-sc-picard-h1-restriction-compatibility] states exactly $c^1H^1(u_j)\alpha_{Z\prime}=\alpha_Z j^*$. Set $\delta=\beta\partial(c^1)^{-1}\alpha_Z$. These canonical homomorphisms define a canonical group homomorphism with precisely the required source and target.

For $[L]\in\operatorname{Pic}(Z)$, invertibility of $\beta$ shows $\delta[L]=0$ exactly when $(c^1)^{-1}\alpha_Z[L]\in\ker\partial$. By Step 3 this holds exactly when it equals $H^1(u_j)(x)$ for some $x\in H^1(Z\prime,\mathcal O_{Z\prime}^{\times})$. Write $x=\alpha_{Z\prime}[M]$ using Step 4; the compatibility there and injectivity of $\alpha_Z$ then say precisely $[L]=j^*[M]$. Thus $\ker\delta=\operatorname{im}j^*$. Every hypothesis used was a closed immersion with square-zero ideal; no finiteness, properness or reducedness was introduced.
